title: Win As Many Rounds Against the Opponent as You Can

concept.title: Spend the cheapest card that still wins; sacrifice your weakest card on the rounds you cannot win
body: You and an opponent each hold `n` cards with numbers on them. You know the order in which the opponent will play his cards, and you may play yours **in any order you like**. In every round the higher card wins; equal cards win nothing. What is the **largest number of rounds** you can win? For your cards `2 7 11 15` against `1 10 4 11` you can win all four rounds: `2` beats `1`, `11` beats `10`, `7` beats `4`, `15` beats `11`.

Because you choose the order freely, the question is a matching: pair each of your cards with a different opponent card so that as many pairs as possible have *your card bigger*. Sort both lists. Look at the opponent's **strongest** card first. If your strongest card beats it, use that card on it, since no weaker card of yours can win this round, and this is the only use of a strong card that cannot be made worse. If your strongest card does not beat it, then **no card** of yours does, so this round is lost anyway, and it should absorb your **weakest** card, because the weakest card is the least useful anywhere else.

body.code:
a.sort(); b.sort()
lo, hi = 0, n - 1                     # my weakest and my strongest remaining card
wins = 0
for j in range(n - 1, -1, -1):        # the opponent's cards from the strongest
    if a[hi] > b[j]:
        wins += 1
        hi -= 1
    else:
        lo += 1                         # a lost round takes my weakest card
print(wins)

body: The program in the editor does the same from the other end: for each of my cards from the weakest, it tries to beat the *weakest unbeaten* opponent card with the *weakest* card that does. Both are the classic "greedy matching" on two sorted lists, with the same O(n log n) cost from the sort.

statement: Two players each have `n` cards. The first player may play his cards in any order; the second plays his in the given order. In every round the higher card wins the round (equal cards: no winner). Print the largest possible number of rounds the first player can win.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of cards each player has.
The second line has `n` numbers: your cards.
The third line has `n` numbers: the cards of the opponent, in the order in which they will be played.
outputFormat: Print the largest number of rounds you can win.

examples.note: All four rounds can be won: 4.

hints: Walk over your cards from the weakest; a card that beats the weakest unbeaten opponent card should be used on it.
A card that cannot win anything is simply skipped.

b = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: Both lists are sorted; each of my cards, from the weakest, is compared with the weakest opponent card that is still unbeaten, and if it wins, that pair is counted and the pointer moves on.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(1) extra.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
b = list(map(int, input().split()))

a.sort()
b.sort()
wins = 0
for x in a:
    if x > b[wins]:
        wins += 1
print(wins)
